outcome_detail: The City of Chicago settled the woman's lawsuit for $100,000, per ProPublica's May 2025 investigation. The settlement date was not reported in available coverage.
criminal_detail: Corey Deanes was arrested in May 2019 and charged with two misdemeanor counts of battery, one felony count of aggravated battery in a public place, and three felony counts of official misconduct for inappropriate physical contact with three women in separate on-duty incidents between August 28, 2017 and July 13, 2018. In 2020 he pleaded guilty to a reduced charge of misdemeanor battery and received two years of probation; he was stripped of his Illinois law-enforcement certification.
incident_date_approx: August 28, 2017 (traffic stop underlying this suit); related incidents through July 2018
description: A 23-year-old woman sued the City of Chicago over an August 2017 traffic stop by Chicago police officer Corey Deanes, a 13-year veteran. According to the lawsuit and reporting, Deanes made inappropriate comments during the stop, threatened to write her a ticket if she did not give him her phone number, hugged her, and touched her buttocks. She reported the incident to the police department and to the Independent Police Review Authority, and police records and the lawsuit indicate investigators took more than a year to interview her. The city settled the suit for $100,000. Deanes was criminally charged in 2019 over on-duty contact with three women and pleaded guilty in 2020 to a reduced charge of misdemeanor battery, receiving two years of probation and losing his state law-enforcement certification.
